notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Tuesday 24 November (EGX30 50,885.33); Wednesday's session has not opened. Brent, gold and Asian stocks are Wednesday-morning prices; Wall Street is Tuesday's close. The pound is the six-bank average at midday Tuesday reported by Amwal Al Ghad. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Wednesday prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Tuesday's net flows by nationality, because Amwal Al Ghad's figures (foreigners selling EGP 25.7 bn, Arabs EGP 5.7 bn, Egyptians buying EGP 31.4 bn) exceed the day's EGP 8.8 bn turnover reported by EnterpriseAM, which names international investors as the only net sellers; a CBE dollar rate (54.17 buy and 54.31 sell appear only in a summary of EnterpriseAM's page); Wednesday's Nikkei and Hang Seng moves, which differ within the same Investing.com page; Samsung and SK Hynix moves, which differ between Investing.com and Al Jazeera; Tuesday's advancing and declining stocks. Egypt Aluminum's 17 November row on StockAnalysis remains inconsistent (a -0.30% change against a 5.2% fall in the closes).
notes.sourcesFoot: All 21 StockAnalysis pages opened on Wednesday morning and show Tuesday 24 November as the latest session.

items: The EGX30 rebounds 1.44% to 50,711.96 on Monday and small caps jump 3.41%, recovering part of Sunday's sell-off → every stock in the 21-stock table except Emaar Misr rises as global markets steady.

Misr Life Insurance opens its IPO book at EGP 12.00 to 13.60 a share, valuing it at EGP 60 to 68 bn → the whole range sits below the EGP 13.82 fair value set by its adviser; trading is due around 3 December.

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang and the Nasdaq jumps 6.5%, its best day since April 2025; Taiwan rises about 9% on Tuesday → the AI trade revives after last week's rout, lifting risk appetite worldwide.
Brent falls 3.46% to $89.37, its lowest close since 31 August, as Libya restarts the Sharara pipeline → cheaper oil eases Egypt's fuel import bill.

The EGX30 drops 2.85% to 49,989.79 on Sunday and small caps fall 5.55%, as local investors sell after Wall Street's correction → foreigners are the only net buyers; turnover stays 40.4% below its 90-day average.
Three LNG cargoes bound for Egypt divert to Europe, and fertiliser makers pay 50% more for gas at $12.75/mmBtu → Europe outbids Cairo for scarce cargoes, raising costs for energy-hungry industry.
US stock futures jump 2.2% on Monday after the S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday into a correction → a rebound abroad could steady the EGX after Sunday's sell-off.
Tankers are set ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi refinery → Gulf attacks keep oil's risk premium alive; Brent holds near $92.7.
Iran strikes US air-defence sites in Bahrain and tankers are hit near Hormuz on Saturday → the Gulf war widens, keeping oil, shipping and insurance risk high for Egypt.
Goldman Sachs sees the CBE holding at 20% until late Q1 2027, then cutting 700 bp by 2028 → it calls the pound more than 30% undervalued and sees no external financing gap through FY2029/30.
Misr Life Insurance, which earned EGP 5.8 bn in 2025, targets a 70% payout ahead of its EGX debut in early December → a large, high-dividend state listing deepens the market.
Orascom Construction breaks ground on Jordan's $6.7 bn Aqaba-Amman water project → the project adds to its backlog before its merger shares list on 24 November.
Wall Street enters a correction: the Nasdaq falls 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.5% on Friday as the AI sell-off deepens → a global risk-off mood can weigh on emerging markets, including the EGX on Sunday.
Gold posts its worst week in eight months, down 8.9%, and 21K gold in Egypt drops 3.04% to EGP 5,575 → markets bet on a December Fed hike, and margin calls force sales.

Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh as Gulf war-risk costs climb → tanker insurance from the Middle East to Asia reaches $12.29 a barrel, keeping Red Sea and Suez risk high.
Arab Energy Fund launches a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → a Gulf-backed buyer puts a price on an EGX-listed oil services firm.
An AI-led sell-off hits markets: the Nasdaq falls 2.3% on Thursday and Asian indices drop up to 6.8% on Friday → Anthropic's record IPO does not calm AI-bubble fears.
Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027 → higher pay supports spending but raises costs for labour-heavy firms.
The EGX30 slips 0.17% to 51,458.04 as Telecom Egypt falls 3.47% → turnover is 43.9% below the 90-day average.
Gold drops to a 14-month low of $3,554 and heads for a 9% weekly loss → markets price a 97.3% chance of a Fed hike in December.

key.l: Houthi-run Red Sea port struck by the Saudi-led coalition

stories.h: Coalition strikes Hodeidah; Houthis threaten Saudi Red Sea ports
stories.what: The Saudi-led coalition says it strikes the Houthi-run port of Hodeidah and two northern Yemeni governorates near the Saudi border. The Houthis had warned they would target all of Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports, including Jeddah, if Hodeidah was attacked. Near Hormuz, three ships were struck on Monday, according to UKMTO.
stories.why: The war between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis escalates alongside the war on Iran.
stories.aff: Red Sea shipping, Gulf ports and insurance costs.
stories.eg: A wider Red Sea war threatens Suez Canal traffic and raises freight costs.
stories.egx: Bearish for shipping and Suez-linked services.

stories.h: AI sell-off resumes as the US threatens new tariffs
stories.what: The Nasdaq falls 1.5% to 23,733.54 and the S&P 500 0.5% to 7,203.38 on Tuesday, while the Dow rises 0.9% to 50,021.91; Nvidia drops 6.5% after Monday's 31.5% jump. On Wednesday Seoul's Kospi falls 6.16% and Taiwan's index 4.94%. The US opens an investigation into excess capacity among 16 trading partners, and a US jury convicts Huawei of conspiring to steal trade secrets.
stories.why: Investors doubt AI spending will pay off, and tariff threats add to the strain.
stories.aff: Global tech stocks and emerging-market risk appetite.
stories.eg: Renewed risk aversion can slow flows into Egyptian assets.

stories.h: EGX30 edges up 0.34% as Sidpec and Orascom Development lead
stories.what: The EGX30 rises 0.34% to 50,885.33 on Tuesday and the EGX70 0.09%; market cap is EGP 4.01 tn. Turnover improves to EGP 8.8 bn, 20.2% below the 90-day average. Sidpec (+5.4%), Orascom Development (+4.6%) and Raya Holding (+3.4%) lead the gainers; AMOC (-2.1%), Qalaa (-2.1%) and Ibnsina Pharma (-1.9%) fall. The index is up 21.7% this year but 10.2% below its 6 September peak.
stories.why: The sources give no single cause for the move.
stories.eg: Buyers return slowly after Sunday's sell-off.

key.l: Misr Life retail cover after day one

stories.h: Misr Life's retail book is a fifth covered on day one
stories.what: Retail investors order about 7.09 mn shares on the first day, 0.19x the 37.5 mn on offer and about EGP 96 mn at the top of the range. Institutions, who take 95% of the 750 mn-share offering, have not disclosed their orders. Misr Insurance Holding hopes to raise EGP 9 to 10.2 bn, with EFG Hermes leading. Separately, MNT-Halan's stabilisation fund buys 20.56 mn shares at EGP 24.50, about EGP 503.8 mn.
stories.why: The offer opens during a volatile week for global and Egyptian stocks.
stories.aff: IPO demand, brokers and the state's divestment plan.
stories.eg: A slow start; the institutional book will decide the outcome.
stories.egx: Neutral until institutional demand is known.

stories.h: Qalaa raises its stake in the Egyptian Refining Company to 27.1%
stories.what: Qalaa Holdings closes its refinery deal early, lifting its stake in the Egyptian Refining Company to 27.1% from 13% alongside an EGP 3.87 bn capital increase. ERC brought in EGP 60.7 bn of Qalaa's EGP 65.9 bn of third-quarter revenue.
stories.why: Qalaa consolidates its hold on its largest source of revenue.
stories.aff: Qalaa's earnings and Egypt's refining sector.
stories.eg: A bigger share of refinery profits flows to an EGX-listed company.

stories.h: Egypt's green hydrogen pipeline shrinks as 20 developers step back
stories.what: Twenty companies step back from green hydrogen projects in Egypt, including firms behind seven of the nine COP27 framework agreements worth up to $83 bn and all seven firms behind a $41 bn set of MoUs from February 2024. Separately, the competition authority refers five suppliers over Alexandria University tenders, and an amended law would raise fines to as much as 15% of revenue.
stories.why: Developers pull back from costly, long-dated projects.
stories.aff: The SCZone, renewable energy and foreign investment pledges.
stories.eg: Fewer large energy projects than announced.
stories.egx: Mildly bearish for contractors tied to the SCZone.

stories.h: Brent rebounds 2.3% on Hormuz attacks, then eases on glut fears
stories.what: Brent rises $2.03, or 2.27%, to settle at $91.40 on Tuesday after touching $88.10, its lowest since 27 August. It slips 1.4% to $90.12 on Wednesday morning. Deutsche Bank estimates oversupply at 1.7 mn barrels a day, and OPEC+ ministers meet on 29 November to set 2027 output.
stories.why: Attacks on ships near Hormuz offset a growing supply surplus.
stories.eg: Brent near $90 keeps Egypt's fuel bill in check.

key.l: odds of a December Fed hike

stories.h: Gold slides back toward 15-month lows on Fed hike bets
stories.what: Spot gold falls 2.2% to settle at $3,556.16 on Tuesday and another 1% to $3,522.68 on Wednesday morning. CME FedWatch shows a 96.4% chance of a 25 bp Fed hike in December, and US PCE inflation data are due on Wednesday. In Egypt, Banky's 21K price falls EGP 10 to EGP 5,570 a gram.
stories.why: Hike bets and a dollar near a 19-month high weigh on gold.
stories.eg: Local gold prices stay near their lows.
